title: Add indication of holiday region
line: With several holiday regions enabled, the clock's event list now shows which region each holiday belongs to.
explanation: The Holidays calendar plugin only set each holiday's name, so with several regions enabled the Digital Clock's event list showed a flat list of names and same-day holidays from different regions couldn't be told apart. The plugin now sets the region's name as the holiday's description when more than one region is selected; the event list already shows descriptions as a second line under the title.

commits.message:
plasmacalendarintegration: show the holiday region when several are enabled

With more than one holiday region selected, the calendar listed every
holiday by name only, so there was no way to tell which region it came
from. Each holiday now shows its region's name as its description then.

BUG: 372044

patches.diff:
From d01992cb898882bebdf0aeae57a58acd0ec7bc32 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 22:28:09 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] plasmacalendarintegration: show the holiday region when
 several are enabled

With more than one holiday region selected, the calendar listed every
holiday by name only, so there was no way to tell which region it came
from. Each holiday now shows its region's name as its description then.

BUG: 372044
---
 plasmacalendarintegration/holidaysevents.cpp | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/plasmacalendarintegration/holidaysevents.cpp b/plasmacalendarintegration/holidaysevents.cpp
index e2e426c103..65176085b4 100644
--- a/plasmacalendarintegration/holidaysevents.cpp
+++ b/plasmacalendarintegration/holidaysevents.cpp
@@ -49,6 +49,9 @@ void HolidaysEventsPlugin::loadEventsForDateRange(const QDate &startDate, const
             eventData.setEndDateTime(holiday.observedEndDate().endOfDay());
             eventData.setIsAllDay(true);
             eventData.setTitle(holiday.name());
+            if (m_regions.size() > 1) {
+                eventData.setDescription(region->name());
+            }
             eventData.setEventType(CalendarEvents::EventData::Holiday);
             eventData.setIsMinor(false);
 
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: United States and Canada enabled, November 11: two holidays with no hint of which region each is from.
Same day: each holiday shows its region (United States, Canada) under its name.
